records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Another example, lock them down at home. Make them wear a mask, right? Create COVID in a lab, make everybody sick, force them to get the jab.

verification.notes: The composite statement combines three claims. COVID-19 caused widespread illness, and governments imposed vaccination requirements on some workers. But WHO's 2025 origins assessment says a laboratory-related event cannot be proven or ruled out because critical data remain unavailable; it does not establish that COVID-19 was created in a lab. The supported and unresolved components make the overall statement mixed.

records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I mean, it had, there was actually a really good article on the spectrum. In the Spectator UK regarding how they tried to establish COVID to mirror a religion.

verification.notes: The Spectator Australia published an article titled 'Covidanity: Australia's new state religion' arguing that COVID compliance resembled a religion and comparing masks and other measures to religious symbols and rituals. However, it was an Australian-edition opinion article and did not establish that COVID-19 itself was intentionally created or established to mirror religion, so Owens's paraphrase overstates it.

sources.title: Covidanity: Australia's new state religion
sources.relevance: The cited Spectator Australia opinion article makes the religion analogy but does not prove intentional establishment of COVID to mirror religion.

records.text: The COVID-19 vaccination effort did not create a vaccine that guarded people against COVID-19.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Go back to COVID, right? Oh, stay at home, save lives. What were they actually doing? We don't know what they were doing. We know what they weren't doing. They weren't creating a vaccine that guarded you against COVID.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. Current WHO and CDC evidence shows COVID-19 vaccines reduce severe disease, hospitalization, and death, although protection against infection and transmission is incomplete and wanes. The blanket claim that vaccination created no vaccine that guarded people against COVID-19 is false.

sources.title: Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) — WHO
